facts.statement: Heyuannia was estimated to be 1.5 meters long and weigh twenty kilograms.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul in 2010 estimated its length at 1.5 metres, the weight at twenty kilograms.

facts.statement: Heyuannia had a short, toothless skull with a steep snout.
facts.quote: Its toothless skull is relatively short with a steep snout.

facts.statement: Heyuannia possessed very short arms and digits, with a reduced first digit.
facts.quote: It had very short arms and digits, and its first digit was reduced.

facts.statement: Heyuannia was the first oviraptorid dinosaur discovered in China.
facts.quote: It was the first oviraptorid found in China; most others were found in neighbouring Mongolia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Heyuannia huangi was found in the Dalangshan Formation near Huangsha, Guangdong.
facts.quote: The holotype, HYMV1-1, was discovered in Guangdong near Huangsha in layers of the Dalangshan Formation.

facts.statement: Thousands of eggs, some likely laid by Heyuannia, were uncovered at the discovery site.
facts.quote: Thousands of eggs have also been uncovered at the site, some of them belonging to the genus and likely laid by Heyuannia.

facts.statement: Fossils attributed to Heyuannia include one specimen that may contain reproductive organs.
facts.quote: Multiple other fossils have been found, including one which may retain possible reproductive organs.

facts.statement: Heyuannia was classified within the family Oviraptoridae by Lü in 2002.
facts.quote: Heyuannia was assigned by Lü to the Oviraptoridae in 2002.

facts.statement: The exact subfamily placement of Heyuannia is uncertain, with later analyses placing it in either Oviraptorinae or Ingeniinae.
facts.quote: Its exact placement within this group is uncertain. Later analyses either resulted in a position in the Oviraptorinae or the Ingeniinae.

facts.statement: The arrangement of Heyuannia eggshells suggests a partially open nest and increased parental care.
facts.quote: The arrangement of the eggshells suggests a partially open nest arrangement for Heyuannia, and also indicates that it engaged in increased parental care.

facts.statement: Heyuannia yanshini was first described as the genus Ingenia yanshini by Rinchen Barsbold in 1981.
facts.quote: H. yanshini was first described and named by Rinchen Barsbold in 1981, as a new genus and species Ingenia yanshini.

facts.statement: Heyuannia lived from 83.6 to 66 million years ago during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
